transcript: Representative Roana went on a trip to the West Bank that turned very controversial when he was detained by Israeli settlers and the IDF and then weirdly attacked by American media and other politicians here when he came back home. So, we're going to talk all about that with Representative Connor who joins us now. Thanks for joining us. >> Thank you, Jen. Thanks for having me. >> No problem. So, uh, Ro, where exactly did you go in the West Bank and why did you go there? I went to see uh Palestine from Palestinian eyes. I had been to Israel three times. I wanted to take one trip to the West Bank to the occupied territories to see uh what uh a part tide there looks like. And I was horrified. We were in Hebrron. We were in uh Umlair. We were we saw the raised village of Zunatada. And we really went to the towns and villages uh across the West Bank. And so there's controversy around whether you got permission to do it or not. So let's dive into that. Number one, I'm not sure that as an American or an American representative, uh, you need permission to go into the West Bank, but that's a literal question as to whether you do from Israel, uh, and and what kind of permission you got and what they're saying about it today. >> First of all, you need a uh, expedited visa. So we contacted the Israeli embassy and we got a visa within about 10 minutes. Uh [clears throat] the irony is that the Israeli government actually escorted us out of the airport. So they uh in terms of this the security in fact one person at the airport was yelling at me saying I've done so much damage to the uh state of Israel because I voted against the aid. Why are they having the security uh help of a member of Congress through the airport and why are they allowing me in? So obviously the Israeli government knew about it and we informed the American embassy and now once you have an American passport with the proper visa uh you can just go through the checkpoint into the West Bank. Uh that's uh the case for everyone and that's what we did. >> So you told American embassy and the American embassy eventually did rescue you from that situation with the IDF which we're going to get to in a second and you've been very complimentary of them for helping you to do that. Uh but the ambassador uh who's of course a head of the embassy uh Mike Huckabe says that you didn't get permission, you didn't tell them, and that it's all your fault. Uh so is he lying? Well, he's just wrong about the fact that we give gave them not only did we give them a heads up in the Israeli embassy a heads up, uh but we gave our State Department a heads up through consular services. I mean, think about the facts. How would I just randomly have the cell phone number of the uh deputy uh chief uh of mission? Uh how would I uh have the uh ability to just get him on the phone if we hadn't had given the State Department and the American embassy uh a heads up? Uh how would we have a visa? You know what Hakabe is really concerned about? What the Israeli government is really concerned about is this precedent that America of Congress would dare to go to see the West Bank from the lens of Palestinians and not from the lens of the Israeli government or the American government in a curated itinerary. And that's really at the crux of what's bothering them. >> Yeah. So that that's exactly where I'm going next. But first to finish off with Ambassador Hugabe. Um so okay, you guys have different versions of the events. yours sounds a lot more credible given that you had their information, you called them, they responded. Uh, but how discouraged are you that the American ambassador seems to be siding with a foreign country and not with an American representative? >> It's very sad. Uh, and uh, I had thought that the American ambassador would just say it's terrible that there was this detainment and uh, we expected investigation. uh we expect uh accountability. Uh I really thought that and I would have thought that Hakabe would just call me up and say is everyone in your delegation safe but that's not the case. And [clears throat] uh the reality is uh that Hakabe's ideology and ideological attachment uh to the greater Israel project. I mean he refers to the occupied West Bank as Judea Samar Sam Samaria uh is uh more important than him standing up for Samaran delegation and what happened to us and he believes the accounts more of the Israeli government and the Israeli settlers than he believes our accounts or the accounts of the New York Times or Reuters or all the journalists who wrote about it. >> Yeah. So that's not surprising to people following the news. Ambassador Huckabe doesn't appear to be our ambassador. He seems to be a complete representative of the Israelis. That's actually startlingly obvious to anyone who's looking at it objectively. He he doesn't defend us at all. He only defends the Israelis. So now let's move to uh Mike Huckabe's actual government. That's the Israeli government. Uh so yeah, let's let's talk about why they are so upset about the trip. [snorts] Um what don't they want Americans seeing in the West Bank? We don't want them seeing that Palestinian Christians are not able to put up Passion of Christ play because all the settlers have taken the land. That uh the Palestinians and Christians and Muslims don't have enough water to wash their clothes or flush their toilet. that in Hebron settlers are throwing rotten tomatoes, rotten vegetables, metal parts, uh ur and acid at the shop owners below who are Palestinian and uh who are living in an apartheid condition that a checkpoints even if you're an American citizen if you're Palestinian you could be beaten uh and accounts of people being beaten that settler violence can strike at any moment vandalizing homes vandalizing uh people and that the IDF takes their died even against American citizens. I mean, it's awful. You have to spend one day there and just be sick to your stomach. >> Is it Is it worse than you expected? >> Yes. Much worse. >> Yeah. >> I I I the violence is much worse. Uh sense I expected people would have two lanes to drive on, that there'd be some roads you couldn't drive on, that uh people would be secondass citizens. I didn't expect that people fear for their lives every time they go out and that the uh IDF is basically totally aligned with the extremist settlers. I I didn't expect that the uh that that people would have urine and acid thrown on them. Uh I didn't expect that settlements uh have taken 80% of the land of a place like uh Beala which is a what used to be majority Christian or Bethlehem is surrounded by 24 illegal settlements the place of Christ's birth. I mean, it was uh jarring and I I certainly didn't expect the audacity of the IDF and uh and extremist settlers to detain an American delegation. >> Yeah. So, there's something curious about that uh reaction to that event. So, I want you to tell us what happened. How did the settlers pull you over? How did the IDF react for those who haven't heard it? But also, the reaction here at home seems to be so what? What? That's like normal. Of course, if you're an American, you should get pulled over at gunpoint by settlers. And the idea that that would be a risk to your safety is absurd. I mean, they all came to give you flowers and and and and rainbows, I assume, or I guess they're saying, and that of course the IDF would agree with the craze settlers and not the American representative. Are any of those things what you expected or would they say otherwise? It doesn't seem like it. They tell us that they're lovely people and that you should have no problems. Then when you run into massive problems, they go, I mean that that that couldn't possibly be the case. So tell us what happened there and and then especially visav the reaction you got at home. >> Well, look, we were at Zun Village. It had been raised to the ground by Ganon Levy, one of the extremist settlers. And as we were there, uh, we were suddenly told, "Go in your van. Go in your van." extremist settlers, one brandishing an M4 American gun, uh started uh walking outside our van, kicking our tires, videotaping us, laughing at us. They had blocked their vehicle in front of our van. And people said, "Well, oh, that's not a detainment. You should have just been able to go." Well, there was only one road out and they blocked that road. How were we supposed to go? I guess we could have tried to swerve around them and had them shoot at us. Uh but obviously that didn't happen. And what what the reaction is is of course that could happen to you in uh in the West Bank. Basically, that uh it's normalized, which is actually not uh an an unfair characterization that uh if you go to the West Bank, you can have extremist uh settlers with M4 guns basically detain you. Uh and it shows the conditions there that Palestinians are having to deal with every time. But then when we called the IDF, they further detained us uh and didn't let us go. and uh settlers kept calling other settlers uh to come detain us uh as well. And it called it was only because we knew the number two person at the American embassy who called the uh Israeli government that the police came and uh dispersed the situation 75 to 90 minutes in. U I I haven't exaggerated. I they never pointed a gun at us, but uh blockading us and brandishing M4s is a pretty scary thing.
